advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the `assert binding_store is not None` guard for the required binding_store with an explicit raise (e.g. ValueError/TypeError) so it survives `python -O`.
evidence: outbound_differ.py:535 `        assert binding_store is not None`
Signature changed from required to `binding_store: BindingStoreProtocol | None = None` (diff)
advisory.finding: `compute_outbound_mutations` guards the now-required `binding_store` in the main mutation loop with `assert binding_store is not None`; under `python -O` (or `PYTHONOPTIMIZE`) assertions are stripped, so a `None` binding_store degrades from a clear AssertionError into an `AttributeError` at `binding_store.get_jira_key(local_id)` on the next line.
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace `assert binding_store is not None` with `if binding_store is None: raise ValueError("binding_store is required for a syncable ticket")`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard `binding_store` in `_compute_outbound_select_absent_gets` consistently with the main loop (skip / raise when None) so the optional-binding_store contract behaves identically at both consumers.
evidence: outbound_differ.py:626 `    for _t in local_tickets if client is not None else ():`
The selector is invoked at outbound_differ.py:467 before the per-ticket loop; the docstring claims None binding_store 'only supports callers whose tickets are all excluded'
advisory.finding: `_compute_outbound_select_absent_gets` dereferences `binding_store.get_jira_key(_lid)` with no `binding_store is not None` guard, unlike the main loop. When called with `binding_store=None`, a non-None `client`, and a syncable (non-excluded) ticket, this raises `AttributeError` in the absent-GET pre-selection — which runs BEFORE the main loop's assert — so the two consumers of the newly-optional binding_store fail inconsistently and earlier than the documented contract implies.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make test_type_skip_excludes_ticket_both_consumers actually distinguish the SKIP path: provide a bound ticket (jira_key + binding_store) that WOULD produce a mutation when NOT excluded, and assert the mutation is absent only under SKIP.
evidence: assert all(m.get("local_id") != "T-1" for m in mutations)
Test passes jira_snapshot `{}` and no client/binding_store, so no create/update mutation for an unbound ticket is produced regardless of the SKIP decision.
Inverted-trace: removing the SKIP exclusion still yields no 'T-1' mutation (the ticket is unbound and jira_snapshot is empty), so the assertion stays green — regression-blindness (criterion d).
advisory.finding: test_type_skip_excludes_ticket_both_consumers is regression-blind: with jira_snapshot={} and no client/bindings, compute_outbound_mutations produces no mutation for T-1 whether or not the SKIP exclusion works, so the assertion cannot detect a regression in the type-granular skip path it claims to cover.
scenarios: A future change breaks the per-project SKIP union in the mutation loop; this test stays green.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a control assertion: with the same ticket bound and NOT SKIP-mapped, assert a mutation IS produced; then with SKIP assert it is absent — so the exclusion is the sole variable.
